title: feat: a loop driver keeps the build loop's steps and stops
headline: A build loop now runs under a script that keeps its steps in order, counts the stops that have a number, and halts with a triage card only the owner's Yes clears, within a bounds file the owner signs. Chained kit scripts run, a deleted project holds nothing, and a Yes asked before the act was tried counts.
alignment: v1.38.0 is step T7 of the v2.0 plan, slice 1: the loop driver and the bounds file, with the carry-overs of build 11 closed in the same release.

items.text: `node .claude/loop.mjs` keeps a build loop's state in the git folder, says the one next step, refuses a step out of order or with no evidence, and needs the owner's Yes, in the session the hooks record, after an owner's step opened.

Fix rounds and canary misses per unit, visual increments (reset only by the owner's check) and CI fixes are counted; at a bounds limit the run halts with a triage card (why, the data, the options), and only the owner's Yes to `loop resume <code>` clears it.

`.claude/bounds.json` lists the loop's steps, which are the owner's, and its limits; install seeds it once, a tool writes it only on the owner's pop-up Yes to that exact edit, and a run on a changed one waits for that Yes.
Loop mode arms only when the owner's latest message is exactly the phrase, sent since it was last off; the hooks halt it on any other owner message and turn it off at session start and a compact.
The kill switch `autonomy-off` now makes every loop step the owner's, as it does every merge.
Two kit scripts in one command (render, then check) are no longer held as a write to a protected file; any other node script, inline code or an option beside one still is.
The forget of a deleted kit project now runs, and clears its record when the folder above it is gone too, while its drive answers; any other command naming it says how to clear it.
items.before: Its record could not be cleared

items.text: An owner's Yes asked before the act was tried now counts when its question names the shell, so it no longer costs a second tap; the owner's latest answer decides, a Yes is for a question quoting one act, and one tap runs once across sessions.
A refused resume or yes says when no session id is set, or when no transcript of that session is kept for the repository.
The release notes audit reads a double hyphen only in prose, so a command quoted with a flag no longer fails a draft the build record wrote.
The CI test check keeps to a time budget, says each step as it starts, and names each test it could not check instead of being cancelled with no report.
Recall v12: key 4 says an answer that first notes there is nothing to push yet still scores when it states the rule (the owner's ruling).
The README says how to retire a kit project: delete its folder, then clear its record with `kit.mjs forget`.

verification: Each fix has a test that fails on 1.37.0 and passes here.
K93, K94 and K96 were reproduced on the released 1.37.0 before the fix; K97's cause was read from the build 11 transcript.

decisions.decision: The loop driver is a kit script, not a native workflow or the built-in loop
decisions.why: Workflows and /loop keep no counters and hold no stop across a compaction; a script both can call keeps the state in the git folder.

decisions.decision: A Yes asked before the act was tried binds only to a shell its question names
decisions.why: The same text does other things in Bash and PowerShell (git rm -r *.log), so a Yes naming no shell still waits for a held try; naming the shell saves the second tap.

upgrading: Run `install user` first, then `install project` in each project. A project gets `.claude/bounds.json` once; edit it only through a pop-up Yes to the exact edit.
limits: The driver counts what it is told: a session that never runs `count` is not stopped by a counter. Watchers, plan self-approval and thread chaining are T7's second slice.

tests.flips: declared tests on v1.37.0 and on this branch; the PR run gives the final count
